note: Withdrawable fact pool for the hardware/telemetry scenario, seeded from public utility/telecom outage-report patterns. Facts paraphrased; each record funds one distinct page. Page limit = number of records.
sources: Public utility/telecom outage report structure (event window, affected firmware, recovery action)

records.description_body: The TGX-9 telemetry gateway at North Ridge dropped 34 percent of inbound sensor packets over a four hour window.
records.timeline_body: A buffer occupancy alarm fired at 02:11; packet loss began at 02:14 and recovered after a manual power cycle at 06:31.
records.contributing_body: Firmware 4.2.1 allocates a fixed inbound buffer that does not scale with packet rate spikes under thermal stress.
records.action: Roll back to firmware 4.1.8 on affected sites, or apply the 4.2.2 hotfix once validated.

records.description_body: The East Mesa gateway dropped 18 percent of telemetry packets over a two hour window before automatic failover engaged.
records.timeline_body: A rate-spike warning preceded the loss by six minutes; failover to the standby unit restored throughput.
records.contributing_body: Sustained inbound packet rate above 12k packets per second overran the fixed buffer on firmware 4.2.1.
records.action: Enable adaptive buffer sizing on 4.2.2 and add packet-rate alerting.

records.description_body: The South Bluff gateway lost 41 percent of packets over a five hour window during a heat advisory.
records.timeline_body: Cabinet temperature reached 43 C; the buffer flush routine slowed and occupancy climbed until a power cycle cleared it.
records.contributing_body: Elevated cabinet temperature compounded the firmware 4.2.0 buffer flush delay.
records.action: Add cabinet thermal monitoring and schedule cooling-fan inspection.

records.description_body: The West Canyon gateway had a brief 9 percent packet loss over a one hour window that self-recovered.
records.timeline_body: A transient occupancy spike cleared without intervention after upstream traffic normalized.
records.contributing_body: A short-lived traffic burst briefly exceeded buffer capacity on firmware 4.2.1.
records.action: Validate the 4.2.2 hotfix in staging before fleet rollout.

records.description_body: The Cedar Flat gateway dropped 27 percent of packets over a three hour window during peak ingest.
records.timeline_body: A queue-depth alarm preceded the loss by four minutes; a scheduled restart restored throughput.
records.contributing_body: Peak ingest exceeded the fixed buffer allocation of firmware 4.2.1.
records.action: Stagger ingest scheduling and roll back to 4.1.8 on peak sites.

records.description_body: The Iron Gate gateway lost 52 percent of packets over a six hour window after a cooling failure.
records.timeline_body: The cabinet cooling fan failed at 01:20; temperature climbed and packet loss persisted until manual cooling was applied at 07:20.
records.contributing_body: A failed cooling fan drove sustained thermal stress that firmware 4.2.0 could not absorb.
records.action: Replace the cooling fan and add redundant thermal sensing.

records.description_body: The Pine Hollow gateway, already on the 4.2.2 hotfix, held throughput during a two hour traffic surge with no packet loss.
records.timeline_body: Adaptive buffer sizing absorbed the surge; occupancy peaked at 78 percent and recovered without intervention.
records.contributing_body: The 4.2.2 hotfix adaptive buffer prevented the loss signature seen on earlier firmware.
records.action: Prioritize the 4.2.2 rollout to remaining sites based on this result.

records.description_body: The Rocky Spur gateway dropped 33 percent of packets over a four hour window mirroring the North Ridge signature.
records.timeline_body: A buffer occupancy alarm at 03:05 preceded loss at 03:09; recovery followed a power cycle at 07:09.
records.contributing_body: The same fixed-buffer limitation of firmware 4.2.1 recurred under thermal load.
records.action: Roll back to firmware 4.1.8 and confirm thermal monitoring is active.
